messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a bunch of tenants have pinned tokens to v1 in the Console. UX question: should pins auto-expire?

sam: leaning toward auto-expire. otherwise pins accumulate and we keep routing to old infra forever.

liam: what would the expiry be? 30/60/90 days? also need a clear telemetry signal when a pin is auto-removed.

katie: +1 for telemetry. also console should show 'pinned until X' so product & users aren't surprised.

anya: proposal: default auto-unpin at 90d for hosted tenants, show badge in Console. But for Dedicated/Private customers, make it opt-in to auto-expire (legal/contracts).

sam: sounds reasonable. we should also emit an event: `pin.expired` with fields {token_id, customer_tier, pinned_version, reason:auto}.

liam: agree on event. add sampling for high-volume tenants to avoid flood? or use telemetry summarization.

katie: Console mock: "Pinned version: v1 — expires in 72 days (auto-unpin)" with a confirmation modal if they re-pin. Include link to migration guide.

anya: rough config in runtime: 
```json
{
  "pin_ttl_days": 90,
  "allow_persistent_pin": false,
  "tiers_exempt_from_auto_unpin": ["dedicated", "private"]
}
```

sam: question: If we auto-unpin, what's the routing behavior for in-flight keys? e.g., sticky caches or client SDKs that expect v1.

liam: runtime should mark a token as 'unpin_pending' and continue honoring sticky route for existing KV-cached connections for up to 10 minutes, then fall back to routing policy (most recent default). We need to surface fallback logs.

katie: UX: show console timeline event: "Auto-unpinned at T, traffic routed to v2 (fallback)" with a link to per-route traces.

ops-bot: deploy-bot noted: "new config `pin_ttl_days` will be added to routing-service v0.9.2 — running canary now" :rocket:

anya: edge-case: what about programmatic pins via API? customers might programmatically re-pin frequently and effectively bypass expiry. Should we rate-limit re-pins?

sam: propose rate-limit: max 1 re-pin per 24h per token unless account has explicit exemption. That prevents churny automation.

liam: also need analytics: count of pinned tokens, avg lifetime, top pinned versions. Hook into Optimize so we can recommend migration recipients.

katie: UX copy: explain why we auto-expire: "Pins can block optimizations, increase cost, and hide deprecations. Auto-expiry keeps apps safe while preserving escape hatch."

anya: ok next steps: 1) eng-platform to add `pin_ttl_days` + `tiers_exempt` flags and telemetry events (sam + liam) 2) Console to add badge + timeline UX + confirm modal (katie) 3) update docs + migration guide + recommended re-pin rate-limit in API docs (product) 4) ops: canary rollout (ops-bot).

sam: i'll open an RFC with config schema and telemetry contract later today.

liam: i'll stub the runtime behavior and tests for sticky caches/unpin_pending.

katie: will mock badges & modal. putting a quick figma link: https://figma.com/s/example-pin-modal

anya: thanks team — tagging @sam @liam @katie for follow-up. will sync next Wed if any blockers. :thumbsup:
